content:
Are we still slaves, or what?

Why is the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court wearing that strange British wig and colonial-era judicial attire while taking the oath?

Is this constitutional?

Have the founding fathers of India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Myanmar done a serious wrong to their citizens by retaining colonial roots in our constitutional spirit?

In this way, does the Constitution itself become unconstitutional in its failure to represent the land and the people of the nation for which it is called the law of the land?

All countries that were historically part of what was called Bharat must rethink: Are we truly free, or can we still think freely?

If we have been thinking in the right direction, why are we still slaves to the British mindset?

Why do Pakistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, and India continue to fight with one another within a network of divisions and conflicts that were created or deepened during the colonial era?

It is time to question our inherited assumptions and re-examine our history, not to erase our separate identities or independence, but to explore whether we can rediscover a common civilisational identity and a peaceful common union among the peoples of the former" Hindustan ie Bharat not India ie Bharat".

No religion or ideology should come in the way. We are brothers.

Yet we continue to fight, often within the very framework of colonial divisions and legacies that shaped our past.

Perhaps true independence does not merely mean removing the foreign ruler.

True independence also means becoming free from the foreign mindset.
